subject: Dashboard action map for QBR: latency, cost, uptime, usage
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, susan@acme.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dashboard action map for QBR: latency, cost, uptime, usage

Team / Susan — dropping the November metric pack and a short ask for QBR prep. We need a concise action map we can present to execs tomorrow: what changed, proposed mitigations, and owners. High-level highlights from this morning's dashboard snapshot (linked below + attached full pack):

- Latency: p50 = 88ms (↑12% vs prior month), p95 = 420ms (↑22%). Notable tail increase between 10:30–12:30 PT on 11/02 correlated with a few heavy-batch model jobs.
- Cost: normalized unit cost ≈ $1,200 / 1M tokens (↑18% month-over-month). Bulk of increase from sustained higher sequence lengths on inference-heavy customers.
- Uptime: 99.92% for the month-to-date; two short incidents (2m and 8m) during the window above — both recovered without rollback.
- Usage: overall request volume up 24% driven by two accounts (Acme AI & QuantumOps) and some internal load tests.

Immediate asks: please respond in-thread with owner commitments by EOD. I want a one-slide summary for execs plus three bullets for each metric: cause, short-term mitigation (≤72h), mid-term fix (30–60d).

Proposed owners (feel free to reassign):
- Latency triage & traces: markus_klein
- Cost analysis + pricing impact: kimberly_park
- Uptime incident notes & RCA draft: jonas_weber
- Customer usage breakdown & outreach for Acme: tessa_morgan

Attachments: QBR_metric_pack.pdf (full dashboards), latency-trace-20261103.csv (sample traces), cost-breakdown-1Mtokens.xlsx.
Links: https://dash.redwood.ai/r/ops/monthly-metrics-202611

Susan — looping you in so you're aware of the current state; we'll surface the one-pager in the QBR.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Platform Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: susan@acme.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dashboard action map for QBR: latency, cost, uptime, usage

Thanks, Irene — quick read and owner ack. I will take latency triage. Initial notes:
- Early signal looks like increased KV-cache churn from longer context windows + a small cohort of requests hitting unoptimized attention kernels. I'm running a targeted trace analysis (attached csv) and will cross-check with the model variants list.
- Short-term mitigation: force-pin the model variant with reduced attention kernel for the high-tail customers and enable a conservative batching cap for 12–24h to avoid tail amplification.
- Mid-term: validate a new kernel selection heuristic in staging (A/B) and prepare a fast rollback path if p50 improves but p95 doesn't.

I'll have a 1-slide technical summary by 14:00 PT and a recommended change set by 18:00 PT.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dashboard action map for QBR: latency, cost, uptime, usage

Irene — I'll take the cost analysis and pricing impact. Early observations:
- The cost delta is concentrated in two places: longer average sequence length for inference (30% ↑ on a small set of customer flows) and a material increase in synchronous low-latency queries that preclude batching.
- Short-term: propose a usage-pricing note we can share with Acme and other large consumers — recommend a temporary rate card for heavy long-context usage or a soft throttling policy applied by customer tier.
- Mid-term: propose a cost-visibility feature in Console (per-route token breakdown) to help customers self-diagnose.

Susan — looping you for transparency. Would you be open to a short customer call this week to review usage spikes? If yes, Tessa, can you coordinate availability?

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
